answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from a capital vault: every agent must stake collateral before it may act, and rewards pay only the address that funded that stake. Registering a thousand sock puppets therefore means posting a thousand separate bonds. An attacker can split a river of fake identities, but each one drains fresh capital, and proven fraud slashes the stake to zero. At that point the cost of a duplicate exceeds its expected yield, so the ledger holds agents backed by real capital, and duplicating an identity never reaches the summit of profitability.
